**Caption:**

PPF and ceramic coating aren't the same thing. One stops the damage. The other repels it.

Paint Protection Film is a physical barrier — a self-healing polyurethane film that sits over your paint and absorbs stone chips, road debris, and car park scrapes before they reach your clear coat.

You don't have to pick one.

## Platform: Facebook

**Caption:**

Here's something most car owners don't know before they buy paint protection: PPF and ceramic coating aren't alternatives — they're two different layers doing two different jobs.

PPF (Paint Protection Film) is a physical film that sits over your paint and absorbs stone chips, road debris, and car park contact. It's self-healing, so minor scuffs disappear on their own. If you drive the South Eastern Freeway or Mornington Peninsula regularly, you already know the sound of a stone hitting your bonnet — PPF stops that from becoming a chip.

Ceramic coating is a chemical bond with your clear coat. It's not a film — it's a nano-ceramic layer that makes your paint hydrophobic, UV-stable, and resistant to bird droppings and contaminants for up to 8 years (9 years on our graphene coating).

The smart move is both: PPF on the high-impact panels first, then ceramic on top. That's the combination we've applied to 2,400+ Melbourne cars across Toorak, Brighton, Richmond, and Bayside.

Just got a new car and wondering which way to go? Message us or book a free consultation online — link in bio.

## Platform: LinkedIn

**Caption:**

Most people think ceramic coating and PPF are two names for the same thing. They're not — and the distinction matters if you're protecting a car worth $50K–$200K.

**Paint Protection Film** is a physical barrier. A self-healing polyurethane film applied over your paint that absorbs stone chips, road debris, and physical contact before any damage reaches the clear coat. On a car that does real Melbourne kilometres — the Eastern Freeway, the Nepean Highway, Mornington Peninsula roads — PPF is the first layer of protection, not an optional upgrade.

**Ceramic coating** is a chemical bond. A nano-ceramic layer fused to your clear coat that makes the surface hydrophobic, UV-stable, and scratch-resistant for years. Manufacturer-backed warranties up to 8 years on ceramic, 9 years on graphene coating. Water sheets off. Bird droppings don't etch. Car park dust doesn't stick.

They work together, not as alternatives. The correct order is PPF on the high-impact panels first, ceramic coating on top for the full surface. That combination is what we apply to Porsche, Ferrari, Tesla, Range Rover, and Mercedes-AMG builds at our Melbourne studio — certified by Ceramic Pro and Gtechniq, not casual installers.

If you own or manage a high-value vehicle and want a clear recommendation on which protection combination fits your car and how you use it, reach out. The consultation is free. The stone chips aren't.
